newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Mar 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Mar 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Eighteen people including four jockeys and two trainers were arrested in a large-scale operation by the Independent Commission Against Corruption in a crackdown on illegal bookmakers and syndicated race fixing.

-- MING PAO -- Government statistics showed that there was an increasing number of pregnant mainland Chinese women who had entered the territory illegally to have their children delivered in Hong Kong.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- The Chinese army had been instructed to study the thrust and spirit of the recent meetings of the National People's Congress and the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and accelerate defence modernisation.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The head of the Special Administrative Region Land Fund Office said that the HK$160 billion fund would be transferred to the future SAR government after the handover so that the Chief Executive could decide how to use it.

-- Sources at the Xinhua News Agency Hong Kong branch said that after the handover, most of the Agency's present functions would remain, and its director would continue to be the highest-ranking Chinese official in Hong Kong.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Britain's former prison inspector would make an unprecedented tour of Hong Kong jails this month to prepare an independent report on penal institutions in the territory.
-- Recent results showed that smaller banks had achieved a first-round victory over larger institutions in last year's price war on residential mortgage rates.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Delegates to the just-ended meeting of China's top advisory body, the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, were for the first time allowed to criticise the government.
-- Xinhua News Agency's Hong Kong branch said it was toning down its rhetoric since the selection of Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa, and probably would be silent after the handover.
